data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for implementing, managing, and enforcing logical access to information systems and granting accounts the least privileges necessary to carry out assigned duties or actions.
It is USDA policy to comply with Federal requirements by establishing, implementing, and enforcing access control policies and procedures.

This policy complies with the requirements of the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq., and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq.

National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: The access control family of controls in the NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, provide the basis for this policy.
cross_references: NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: This policy serves as guidance for agencies to develop and implement access control procedures that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements.
This policy supersedes:
DR 3505-003, Access Control Policy, February 10, 2015, in its entirety; and
cross_references: DR 3505-003, Access Control Policy, February 10, 2015, in its entirety

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3505-002, Wireless Networking Security Policy, August 11, 2009, in its entirety.
cross_references: DR 3505-002, Wireless Networking Security Policy, August 11, 2009, in its entirety

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded or expired.
All agencies will align their access control policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.target: their access control policies and procedures
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: Terminology used in this DR is defined in Appendix B, Definitions, and Appendix E, Discussion on Logical Access Control Terms.

Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) and United States Government Common Baseline (USGCB) configuration checklists are available from the NIST, National Checklist Program Repository.
cross_references: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG)
United States Government Common Baseline (USGCB) configuration checklists

policy_statements.source_text: When this DR requires application of a setting to comply with a DISA STIG setting, an equivalent setting from a USGCB checklist is also permitted, without waiver.
conditions: When this DR requires application of a setting to comply with a DISA STIG setting

policy_statements.source_text: In this DR, the terms “agency,” “agencies,” “USDA agency,” or “USDA agencies,” when used generically, will be understood to include USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices collectively, unless otherwise specified.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when used generically
unless otherwise specified

policy_statements.source_text: This policy provides guidance for developing and implementing logical access controls for USDA information systems and components of USDA information systems.
policy_statements.target: USDA information systems and components of USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Controlling individual and software access and privileges to information and information systems is required to protect USDA personnel, missions, and business processes against malicious and unauthorized activities.
This policy applies to:
All USDA agencies, employees, contractors, affiliates, interns, volunteers, and fellows who work for, or on behalf of, USDA;
policy_statements.target: USDA agencies, employees, contractors, affiliates, interns, volunteers, and fellows

policy_statements.source_text: All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA;
All information systems or services (including cloud-based services) owned, used, or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA; and
policy_statements.target: information systems or services (including cloud-based services)

policy_statements.source_text: Interconnections between or among these information systems.
policy_statements.target: Interconnections between or among these information systems

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is closely related to other USDA policies, programs, and procedures, including:
DR 3xxx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming;
cross_references: DR 3xxx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: DR 35xx-xxx, Identification and Authentication, forthcoming;
DR 3520-002, Configuration Management, August 12, 2014;
DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices, November 30, 2018;
cross_references: DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices, November 30, 2018

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3580-005, Securing Client Devices for International Travel, November 30, 2018; and
cross_references: DR 3580-005, Securing Client Devices for International Travel, November 30, 2018

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management, December 9, 2011.
cross_references: DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management, December 9, 2011

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems such as those identified in FISMA, policies and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or intelligence community policies, directives, and instructions.
Agencies will develop, implement, and maintain agency processes and procedures aligned with this DR to manage access to USDA information and information systems, ensuring the procedures:

Grant access only to individuals who have an established need-to-know and who meet the minimum interim or full background investigation requirements consistent with the system and level of access being requested;
conditions: who have an established need-to-know and who meet the minimum interim or full background investigation requirements consistent with the system and level of access being requested

policy_statements.source_text: Include monitoring and periodic validation of accounts and privileges;
Specify remedial actions for violations; and
Are reviewed annually and updated, if necessary.
conditions: annually
if necessary

policy_statements.source_text: Logical access controls must:
Be implemented in compliance with Federal, Departmental, and, if applicable, agency policies; and
Restrict access to USDA information, information technology (IT) resources, information systems, and their components to authorized subjects.
Agencies may develop and implement information security policies that meet or exceed the corresponding Departmental policy requirements.
conditions: that meet or exceed the corresponding Departmental policy requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Agency policies cannot be less stringent than Departmental policy requirements.
Specific policy requirements that cannot be fully implemented require an approved waiver (see section 25, Policy Exceptions.)
Agencies will:
Ensure that system security plans (SSP) reference processes for authorizing accounts and assigning access privileges;
Identify and document the account types that are permitted for each USDA information system;
Ensure user accounts issued by USDA are managed based on user identity and position data (e.g., the user role on the information system) from an authoritative source;
Ensure that USDA information system user account records are:
Subject to electronic discovery (ediscovery) in accordance with DR 3090-001, Litigation Retention Policy for Documentary Materials including Electronically Stored Information; and
cross_references: DR 3090-001, Litigation Retention Policy for Documentary Materials including Electronically Stored Information

policy_statements.source_text: Archived in accordance with the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedule 3.2: Information Systems Security Records.
cross_references: General Records Schedule 3.2: Information Systems Security Records

policy_statements.source_text: Assign one or more USDA personnel to serve as the account manager and System Owner’s representative for each USDA information system, with the responsibility for authorizing account actions, such as creating, modifying, disabling, and deleting accounts; and
Establish conditions for role, account, and group membership for each USDA information system, adhering to the principles of least privilege for each.
policy_statements.target: conditions for role, account, and group membership

policy_statements.source_text: Account management processes will ensure that the system owner or designated representative verifies that:
The information provided with each account access request (including modifications) is correct and accurate;
Federal, Departmental, and agency access requirements (including interim standards, if applicable) have been met to grant the requested access;

If any access requirements (e.g., background investigation, position suitability or fitness) have not been met, access to the information system will not be granted, or if already granted, will be disabled;
conditions: If any access requirements (e.g., background investigation, position suitability or fitness) have not been met

policy_statements.source_text: Requests to add or change information system user account accesses or privileges meet the requirements of the information system, as defined by the system owner; and
Account requests are submitted promptly to:
Create accounts, add group members, and assign access privileges;
Modify user accounts, group memberships, and access privileges when a user’s work assignment changes the type of information or information system the user needs to access; or
conditions: when a user’s work assignment changes the type of information or information system the user needs to access

policy_statements.source_text: Disable accounts and remove group memberships when a user transfers or terminates employment, in accordance with agency procedures.
conditions: when a user transfers or terminates employment

policy_statements.source_text: Before authorizing the requested access, account managers will:
conditions: Before authorizing the requested access

policy_statements.source_text: Validate the required description and justification of each role, account, or group privilege requested;
For new user requests, verify the individual’s current background investigation status (including adjudication, if applicable), background investigation type, and the date that it was completed;
conditions: For new user requests

policy_statements.source_text: For all requests, validate that the identified background investigation:
conditions: For all requests

policy_statements.source_text: Meets the minimum (or interim) requirements for the system and level of access requested;
Is still valid and does not require re-investigation or has otherwise lapsed; and
Verify through the Office of Homeland Security (OHS) or personnel security staff, that:
The full investigation has been submitted to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) for adjudication; and

If granting limited interim access to begin work pending adjudication of the required background investigation, that a fingerprint check is completed with no derogatory results, in accordance with Departmental Manual (DM) 4620-002, Common Identification Standard for U.S. Department of Agriculture Employees and Contractors.
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 4620-002, Common Identification Standard for U.S. Department of Agriculture Employees and Contractors

policy_statements.source_text: For new users, verify that individuals have completed computer security awareness training for the current fiscal year, prior to authorizing user access, and current users complete this training annually thereafter, in accordance with DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness and Training Policy;
conditions: For new users
prior to authorizing user access
cross_references: DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness and Training Policy

policy_statements.source_text: Verify annually that individuals requesting or currently holding privileged accounts have completed any required specialized role-based training;
conditions: annually

policy_statements.source_text: Verify that individuals have formally agreed to abide by the system’s rules of behavior and terms of use for the current fiscal year, both initially and annually thereafter; and
conditions: for the current fiscal year
both initially and annually thereafter

policy_statements.source_text: Verify that individuals will use multifactor authentication methods identified in Section 7a(2) to access USDA information systems.

Account managers will only authorize requests to create, modify, disable, or delete information system accounts or access privileges following formal authorization by the system owner, employee manager, or contracting officer’s representative (COR).
policy_statements.target: requests to create, modify, disable, or delete information system accounts or access privileges
conditions: following formal authorization by the system owner, employee manager, or contracting officer’s representative (COR)

policy_statements.source_text: Agency monitoring processes will:
Include audits of all accounts, groups, and roles to ensure account management procedures produce accurate and timely changes.
The objectives of the monitoring and audit activities are to:
Validate with the system owner the continued business needs for each user to access active accounts or groups and ensure that accounts and groups are disabled or removed when no longer needed; and
Reconcile active accounts, groups, and roles with account or role requests, and immediately correct or revoke any accounts or privileges not approved through the account management process.
If necessary, make corrective changes to the procedures, documentation process, or require additional process training for personnel responsible for enforcing the process.
The frequency for audits will be as follows:
Privileged user accounts/groups each quarter (or a portion of the accounts/groups more frequently);
Non-privileged user accounts/groups at least annually; and
Any other accounts (e.g., shared, system, service) or groups not included in Sections 6e(2)(a) and (b), at least annually.
USDA information systems with a high-impact categorization will use account monitoring capabilities to identify and alert on malicious, risky, or atypical account activity.
policy_statements.target: malicious, risky, or atypical account activity
conditions: with a high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: USDA information systems with a moderate- or high-impact categorization will employ an automated mechanism in the process that provides notifications to the account manager to support the management of information system accounts and to audit account usage.
conditions: with a moderate- or high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA information systems will employ an automated mechanism in processes that:
Disable temporary and emergency accounts within 5 workdays of when they are no longer in use or when they have expired;
conditions: within 5 workdays of when they are no longer in use or when they have expired

policy_statements.source_text: Disable public-facing, non-USDA personnel accounts within time periods set by the agency (each information system may have a different time period);
Disable all other inactive privileged accounts within 30 calendar days, and non-privileged accounts within 60 calendar days.
conditions: within 30 calendar days
within 60 calendar days

policy_statements.source_text: Information systems with a business need to keep non-privileged accounts inactive longer will be documented in the SSP; and
conditions: with a business need to keep non-privileged accounts inactive longer

policy_statements.source_text: Create audit records of account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions, and notifies the account manager of these actions.
Agency procedures will require that the credentials (e.g., password) for shared accounts be changed immediately when a member of the group is removed.
conditions: when a member of the group is removed

policy_statements.source_text: USDA information systems with a high-impact categorization will have a process for disabling an account and privileges within a defined amount of time that a user’s access is identified as posing a significant risk to the organization, the information system, other organizations, or the Nation, based on reliable evidence or intelligence.
conditions: with a high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: The amount of time for disabling accounts is determined by the agency, based in part on their infrastructure and capabilities.
USDA information systems will employ discretionary and mandatory access enforcement mechanisms to implement access control policies to ensure that:
Only authorized subjects may access objects in accordance with information system access control policies.
For example, only authorized individuals and software components may access specific information and information resources; and
User access to a USDA information system is authenticated using a multifactor authentication method in accordance with DR 3640-001.

USDA personnel will use a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card, PIV-Interoperable card, or PIV-derived credentials to access USDA information systems, per Office of Management and Budget (OMB) mandates.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) mandates

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies may choose to implement a multifactor authentication solution for the non-USDA workforce, in accordance with DR 3640-001.

Agencies will use SSPs to identify and document system functions, privileged commands, accesses, and other specified actions that require dual authorization; and enforce the dual authorization controls for those actions.
policy_statements.target: system functions, privileged commands, accesses, and other specified actions

policy_statements.source_text: Information systems with moderate- or high-impact categorization will implement information flow control measures to:
conditions: with moderate- or high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: Enforce where and how information is allowed to travel within an information system and between interconnected information systems;
Enforce remote access restrictions;
Encrypt sensitive Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) such as personally identifiable, export controlled, and other protected information from being transmitted as cleartext; and
Prevent unauthorized communication between designated sources and destinations (e.g., individuals, devices, networks).
Agencies will implement the following requirements for information systems categorized as moderate- or high-impact:
conditions: for information systems categorized as moderate- or high-impact

policy_statements.source_text: Document critical functions or privileged actions that require two or more individuals to implement;

Separate duties to reduce the potential risks of any one individual abusing their authorized privileges for malicious purposes, by limiting the range of privileged actions an individual can perform unilaterally;
Enforce information system access authorizations to separate duties for mission functions and information system support functions; and
Ensure that privileged users permitted to manage access control functions cannot alter audit functions or audit records.
Individuals and system processes will have only the minimum privileges necessary to accomplish their assigned tasks.
USDA information systems categorized as moderate- or high-impact will implement the principles of least privilege, ensuring that:
conditions: categorized as moderate- or high-impact

policy_statements.source_text: Principals of least privilege are applied throughout the information system lifecycle (e.g., development, implementation, operational, and disposal phases);

Privileged users permitted to access security functions in hardware, software, or firmware, and security relevant information will use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing non-security features;
conditions: when accessing non-security features

policy_statements.source_text: Privileged accounts and groups are only used to perform privileged job functions;

USDA information systems create audit records when a privileged command is performed, or a privileged account makes a security-related change to a USDA information system, such as creating an account or group, assigning roles and privileges to an account or group, or changing account or group privileges; and
conditions: when a privileged command is performed, or a privileged account makes a security-related change to a USDA information system

policy_statements.source_text: Configuration settings in USDA information systems prevent non-privileged users and accounts from executing privileged functions, including disabling, circumventing, or altering security safeguards and countermeasures, such as performing system integrity checks or cryptographic key management activities.
For USDA information systems with a high-impact categorization, agencies will:
conditions: For USDA information systems with a high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: Only authorize remote network access to privileged commands for compelling operational needs;
Document the specific privileged commands authorized to be executed remotely; and
Provide the rationale for each authorized circumstance.
USDA information systems will use the most current DISA STIG settings to:
Limit the number of unsuccessful login attempts at either the operating system level, the application level, or both; and
Set time limits for the maximum consecutive invalid login attempts.
policy_statements.target: time limits for the maximum consecutive invalid login attempts

policy_statements.source_text: When the maximum number of consecutive unsuccessful login attempts is exceeded during the specified timeframe:
conditions: When the maximum number of consecutive unsuccessful login attempts is exceeded during the specified timeframe

policy_statements.source_text: The account, application, or client device will automatically lock and remain locked for the time specified by the DISA STIG setting or until released by an administrator; and
Agencies may establish a process to manually unlock accounts prior to the expiration of the lockout period after sufficient user identification has been established.
conditions: after sufficient user identification has been established

policy_statements.source_text: Note: The PIV issuance office manages the settings and recovery process for PIV credentials; therefore, settings related to PIV credentials are outside the scope of this policy.
USDA mobile devices will be configured to purge information stored on them:
Unless the devices access network resources from a remote location via the USDA virtual private network (VPN) and those devices employ the same controls as those applied to local devices; and
The devices are protected with sufficiently strong encryption mechanisms.
USDA information systems will display a USDA-approved notification banner at logon before granting individuals access to information systems owned by, or operated on behalf of, USDA.
conditions: at logon before granting individuals access to information systems owned by, or operated on behalf of, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: An example of a notification banner, approved by the Office of the General Counsel (OGC), is in Appendix D.
The notification banner will remain on the screen until the individual acknowledges the usage conditions and takes explicit action to log on to the USDA information system.
Note: Information systems accessible through single sign-on sessions (e.g., SharePoint) may not need to display an additional notification banner.
The banner will provide privacy and security notices consistent with requirements in applicable Federal laws, EOs, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and other guidance.
The notification banner will inform the user that:
They are accessing a U.S. Government information system;
Usage of the information system may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit by the U.S. Government and that users should have no expectation of privacy;
Unauthorized use of U.S. Government information systems is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties;
Use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording; and
Proceeding to the login screen constitutes the individual’s acceptance of all terms and conditions in the banner.
Agencies will configure systems to deny access to any individual who refuses to accept the terms and usage conditions presented in the banner.
policy_statements.target: any individual who refuses to accept the terms and usage conditions presented in the banner

policy_statements.source_text: For publicly accessible USDA information systems:
Agencies may define additional conditions for displaying a notification banner;
The information system will display a public use notification banner before granting further access to the information system; and
The notification banner will include:
A statement that the user is accessing a U.S. Government information system;
System use information and specified usage conditions;
A description of authorized uses of the system; and
Notice of the U.S. Government’s right to monitor, record, or audit activities on the system, consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems, and citations to relevant governing authorities.
Notification banners that deviate from the example in Appendix D must be submitted to the USDA OGC for approval prior to implementation.
conditions: that deviate from the example in Appendix D
prior to implementation

policy_statements.source_text: This control addresses concurrent sessions on a single information system (with a high-impact categorization).
It does not address concurrent sessions by a single user to multiple information systems.
USDA information systems with a high-impact categorization will:
conditions: with a high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: Prevent non-privileged user accounts from logging into more than one concurrent privileged session;
Prevent non-privileged user accounts from logging into more than two concurrent non-privileged sessions; and
Permit privileged user accounts to concurrently login to no more than one privileged and two non-privileged sessions.
Information systems typically implement session locks at the operating system level using screen savers; however, applications can also provide session locking capabilities.
Users should only use session locks for short periods of inactivity and log off the system for long periods, such as at the end of the workday.

USDA information systems will be configured to ensure that after the DISA STIG-specified timeframe of inactivity, an information system or client device automatically initiates a session lock to prevent further access.

Agencies will either require individuals to initiate a session lock, such as a screen lock, when they leave their client device unattended or agency-owned client devices to initiate a session lock when the user removes the PIV card from the client device.
conditions: when they leave their client device unattended
when the user removes the PIV card from the client device

policy_statements.source_text: USDA information systems and client devices will maintain the session lock until the user re-authenticates to the information system or device using established USDA identification and authentication procedures in accordance with DR 3640-001.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA information systems and client devices
conditions: until the user re-authenticates to the information system or device using established USDA identification and authentication procedures in accordance with DR 3640-001

policy_statements.source_text: During a session lock, USDA information systems and client devices will conceal information previously visible on display screens by displaying publicly viewable images that will not contain CUI.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA information systems and client devices
policy_statements.target: information previously visible on display screens
conditions: During a session lock

policy_statements.source_text: The publicly viewable images may be static or dynamic, such as screen savers, blank screens, photographic images, or display non-sensitive device information such as the current time and remaining battery life.
Agencies may not exempt session lock requirements for all accounts on an information system or service.
When there is a mission need to exempt specific accounts from implementing session lock requirement, agencies will document those accounts and rationale in the SSP.
conditions: When there is a mission need to exempt specific accounts from implementing session lock requirement

policy_statements.source_text: Session termination ends all processes associated with a user’s logical session except for those processes that the user specifically created to continue after terminating the session.
Logical sessions are terminable without terminating the network session.
The following requirements apply to USDA information systems with a moderate- or high-impact categorization:
conditions: with a moderate- or high-impact categorization

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will specify in the SSP the conditions and trigger events that result in the termination of a user’s session;
policy_statements.target: conditions and trigger events that result in the termination of a user’s session

policy_statements.source_text: USDA information systems will automatically terminate and require re-authentication to re-establish a user-initiated logical session:
After 30 minutes of inactivity; and
After the occurrence of agency-specified conditions or trigger events.
Agencies will not waive session termination requirements systemwide.
If there is a mission need to exempt one or more system accounts from implementing session termination, the agency will request a waiver for the specific accounts or devices.
conditions: If there is a mission need to exempt one or more system accounts from implementing session termination

policy_statements.section_title: Permitted Actions without Identification or Authentication
policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will identify actions that users may perform on information systems without requiring user identification and authentication and document them in SSPs.
policy_statements.target: actions that users may perform on information systems without requiring user identification and authentication

policy_statements.section_title: Permitted Actions without Identification or Authentication
policy_statements.source_text: Actions that may not require identification and authentication include accessing publicly available USDA websites, answering incoming phone calls, replying to text messages on USDA-issued mobile devices, and receiving fax transmissions on networked fax machines or all-in-one printers.

policy_statements.section_title: Permitted Actions without Identification or Authentication
policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will identify and document in the SSP any action that may exist that are exempt from the identification and authentication requirements under certain circumstances, such as in an emergency.

Remote access encompasses any connection to a USDA information system or component originating from outside of a USDA owned and operated network infrastructure, such as accesses for telework and mobile work.

Access to USDA information systems using Government furnished laptops and mobile devices while on domestic travel will meet the requirements in DR 3580-004, or while on international travel will meet the requirements in DR 3580-005.
Agencies will identify the approved remote access methods for users to access agency information systems.
Agencies will establish usage restrictions, configuration and connection requirements, and implementation guidance for the permitted remote access methods and document them in the SSP.
Remote access requirements will not apply to users accessing USDA public web servers and other publicly accessible systems.

Agencies will ensure that USDA information systems that allow remote access include automated monitoring capabilities to detect and control access attempts by auditing remote access connection activities on a variety of devices.
policy_statements.target: USDA information systems that allow remote access

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will ensure that remote access methods:
Employ NIST FIPS PUB 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules certified encryption and mutual authentication;
cross_references: NIST FIPS PUB 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules

policy_statements.source_text: Route all remote access sessions through a limited number of USDA Trusted Internet Connection network-access control points;
Permit connections to USDA remote client devices only after verifying the client device has been scanned for malware;
Employ a multifactor authentication method identified in Section 7a(2); and
Transmit and transfer data via an encrypted VPN in compliance with DM 3530-005, Encryption Security Standards.
Agencies will document and set conditions (e.g., VPN, encrypted channel) for the execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access methods.
policy_statements.target: execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access methods

policy_statements.source_text: Before allowing wireless connections, each wireless technology used to access a USDA information system will:
conditions: Before allowing wireless connections

policy_statements.source_text: Be authorized by the Mission Area Assistant Chief Information Officer (CIO), or designee;
Identify usage restrictions, configuration and connection requirements, and implementation guidance and document them in the SSP; and

Only permit wireless access authentication protocols that provide mutual device authentication and protect the confidentiality and integrity of user authentication credentials by implementing encryption technologies in accordance with DM 3530-005.
Agencies will identify and explicitly authorize users approved to independently configure wireless networking capabilities, such as:
policy_statements.target: users approved to independently configure wireless networking capabilities

policy_statements.source_text: Permitting users to configure their USDA client device to connect to home networks and to peripheral devices as indicated in DR 3580-004; and
Permitting network administrators to configure USDA wireless access points and wireless settings for USDA backbone servers and devices.

Access enforcement mechanisms will be configured to prevent unauthorized changes to wireless networking capabilities (see DR 3580-004 for additional guidance to allow users some capabilities to manage wireless protocols).

USDA client devices will be configured with the strongest Bluetooth security and encryption modes supported by the device, as discussed in NIST SP 800-121, Revision 2, Guide to Bluetooth Security, and have auto-pairing functionality disabled.
policy_statements.target: strongest Bluetooth security and encryption modes supported by the device
cross_references: NIST SP 800-121, Revision 2, Guide to Bluetooth Security

policy_statements.source_text: USDA client devices will be configured to prohibit connections to multiple networks simultaneously (e.g., disable a laptop’s wireless capability when it is connected to a wired network).

USDA information systems that are wireless-capable, categorized as high impact, and located within Government owned or controlled buildings will implement strategies to minimize the unauthorized access to or use of Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11 wireless communications from outside of USDA facilities, by:
cross_references: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11
conditions: that are wireless-capable, categorized as high impact, and located within Government owned or controlled buildings

policy_statements.source_text: Calibrating radio antennas to reduce transmission power and signal strength;
Employing electromagnetic shielding measures to control wireless emanations; or
Using beam-forming antennas.

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: The requirements in this section apply to USDA-owned or USDA-controlled client devices issued by agencies.
policy_statements.target: USDA-owned or USDA-controlled client devices issued by agencies

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Section 20 provides access requirements for client devices that are not USDA-owned or controlled.

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will:

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Establish usage restrictions; device identification, integrity, and configuration requirements in accordance with DR 3520-002; authentication and connection requirements; and implementation guidance for each type of laptop and mobile device consistent with DR 3580-004;

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Implement anti-malware software and firewalls in accordance with DR 3575-002, System and Information Integrity, including updating anti-malware software and scanning for malware;

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Scan for misconfigurations and current and missing software updates and patches in accordance with DR 3530-006, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities; and
cross_references: DR 3530-006, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Disable unauthorized or unnecessary mobile capabilities, such as wireless and infrared device capabilities.

policy_statements.section_title: Access Control for Mobile Devices and Laptops
policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will ensure that all Government furnished laptops and mobile devices that connect to USDA information systems employ encryption in accordance with DR 3580-004.
policy_statements.target: all Government furnished laptops and mobile devices that connect to USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: External information systems include personally owned devices, such as bring your own device (BYOD).
Agencies that allow BYOD will adhere to the requirements in DR 3xxx-xxx, the BYOD policy.
conditions: that allow BYOD

policy_statements.source_text: Requirements in this section do not apply to external information systems that access public interfaces to USDA information systems, including publicly accessible USDA websites.

Information systems managed by other Federal Agencies or other governmental organization (e.g., state, local, tribal) will be treated as external information systems when they do not have an established trust relationship (e.g., memorandum of agreement or interconnection security agreement) with USDA.
policy_statements.target: Information systems managed by other Federal Agencies or other governmental organization (e.g., state, local, tribal)
conditions: when they do not have an established trust relationship (e.g., memorandum of agreement or interconnection security agreement) with USDA

policy_statements.source_text: All non-Government furnished information systems will be treated as external information systems and adhere to the requirements in DR 3580-004, prior to allowing access to USDA information systems.
conditions: prior to allowing access to USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will only permit authorized individuals to access an external information system or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information when an approved information system connection or processing agreement has been established with the external information system provider.
conditions: when an approved information system connection or processing agreement has been established with the external information system provider

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will prohibit the connection of USDA-controlled removable media to external information systems.
policy_statements.target: connection of USDA-controlled removable media to external information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Additional guidance about removable media can be found in DR 3580-005.
Factors for agencies to consider when developing information sharing procedures include:
Ensure personnel involved in the information sharing process are trained on their roles (i.e., for marking, handling, or sharing sensitive information or CUI), as needed;

Agency procedures may require qualified personnel to review or approve information prior to being released, or may require a signed memorandum of agreement with an external party prior to sharing the information;
Note: The NARA website, CUI Registry: Limited Dissemination Controls, provides dissemination principles.
Other NARA website references in Appendix A provide training about CUI that may be useful in information sharing procedures.

Agency procedures may also, for example, require information systems to display or print information markings, enforce dual authorization requirements prior to electronically transferring information, or enforce sharing restrictions based on signed agreements.
Agencies with information systems categorized as moderate or high impact will additionally develop and implement procedures to:
conditions: with information systems categorized as moderate or high impact

policy_statements.source_text: Facilitate information sharing by enabling authorized users to determine whether requests for access to information they control meet the criteria for granting access to others (i.e., determine whether information with a restriction such as privileged medical, contract sensitive, or classified can be shared with a person internal or external to USDA); and
Implement manual processes or automated mechanisms to assist users in making information sharing and collaboration decisions.
Agencies will explicitly designate individuals authorized to post information on publicly accessible USDA information systems.
policy_statements.target: individuals authorized to post information on publicly accessible USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will develop and implement processes to:
Train authorized users to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain non-public information;
Ensure only authorized users post information approved for public release;
Ensure information intended for public release is reviewed prior to it being posted on a publicly accessible information system;
Conduct monthly reviews of publicly accessible information systems for non-public information; and
Remove non-public information from publicly accessible systems when discovered, maintain a log of the information removed, and institute measures to prevent a recurrence.
conditions: when discovered

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Ensure that Departmental policy and delegations of authority for access control are developed and implemented in support of this DR; and
policy_statements.target: Departmental policy and delegations of authority for access control

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure agencies have adequate resources to carry out access control requirements.
The USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) will:
Ensure the development and maintenance of Departmental access controls in accordance with this DR;
Maintain oversight to ensure the Department and agencies develop, maintain, and comply with policies, procedures, and access control techniques; and
Ensure Mission Area Assistant CIOs, CISOs, and Information Systems Security Program Managers (ISSPM) receive updated Federal and Departmental access control requirements and guidance.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, CISOs, and Information Systems Security Program Managers (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CIOs will:
Assign responsibilities to support and implement this policy;
Ensure policies, procedures, guidance, processes, and checklists, as appropriate, are developed;
Ensure the resources needed to maintain secure local and remote access capability are included in each USDA agency IT budget; and
Approve the use of wireless technologies, mobile devices, and accessories used to connect with information systems.
policy_statements.target: use of wireless technologies, mobile devices, and accessories used to connect with information systems

policy_statements.source_text: CISOs and ISSPMs will:
Provide guidance and enforce the policies, procedures, processes, and checklists developed to comply with this policy;
policy_statements.target: policies, procedures, processes, and checklists developed to comply with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the access control procedures, processes, and checklists are reviewed and, if necessary, updated;
Ensure that access controls are reviewed, appropriately tested, and, if necessary, promptly corrected;
Ensure the security controls to external information systems maintain an acceptable level of risk to information and information systems;
Ensure access control requirements are documented and submitted to the USDA CISO for inclusion in Departmentwide compliance reporting, as needed;
Ensure access control standards including methods, technology, devices, configurations, and tools balance risk and business needs;
Advise system owners about the secure implementation of wireless technologies;
Ensure that staff involved with controlling access to information and information systems are appropriately trained in accordance with DR 3545-001 and authorized to perform those duties;
Ensure auditing is enabled and audit records are created for all account and privilege activities; and
Ensure that privileged users cannot make unauthorized changes to audit settings.
System Owners or Account Managers will:

Ensure the processes to create, maintain, revoke, and verify access controls and privileges implement the security concepts of need-to-know, least privilege, and separation of duties to produce accurate and desired results, and comply with this policy;
Maintain information for all applicable system accounts, and ensure account deactivation when individuals no longer require access;
Approve the roles, accounts, groups, and appropriate privileges assigned to each to implement on information systems;
policy_statements.target: roles, accounts, groups, and appropriate privileges assigned to each

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with information stewards to decide who has access to the information system and determine the types of privileges and access rights;
Approve any accounts exempt from the automatic disabling function;
policy_statements.target: any accounts exempt from the automatic disabling function

policy_statements.source_text: Establish criteria for authorizing and reviewing account types, privileges, roles, and account and group memberships;
Ensure that USDA information systems implement appropriate access control mechanisms, including both discretionary and mandatory access controls;
Ensure assignment of, or changes to, user access and privileges to information systems are implemented only with approved authorizations;
Ensure that privileged accounts are associated with a specific user unless a shared system or service account is required and is specifically authorized;
conditions: unless a shared system or service account is required and is specifically authorized

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that users, including information system support staff, are trained before being granted access to the information system, in accordance with DR 3545-001;
conditions: before being granted access to the information system

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure users formally agree to abide by the system’s rules of behavior and terms of use prior to gaining information system access; and
conditions: prior to gaining information system access

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that staff involved with access controls are appropriately trained and are authorized to manage access.
Information Stewards will:
Provide input to system owners regarding:
The roles that have access to information and their privileges; and
The security requirements and controls needed to protect information where it is processed, stored, or transmitted.

Establish rules for appropriate use and protection of information in information sharing environments and retain that responsibility even when the information is shared with, or provided to, other organizations.
Managers or Supervisors will:
Request new, modified, or terminated access to information systems for employees and other USDA personnel; and
Apply the security concepts of need-to-know, least privilege, and separation of duties when requesting creation or modification of user account accesses and privileges.
CORs will:
Maintain an accurate position description for each contract position;

Submit, in advance of contractor work or access, the necessary information to initiate or verify the contractor’s background investigation, commensurate with the sensitivity described in the position description and the systems and level of access the contractor will require;
Request new, modified, or terminated access for contractor personnel to information systems; and
Apply the security concepts of need-to-know, least privilege, and separation of duties when requesting creation or modification of user account accesses and privileges.
System and Network Administrators will:
Implement and maintain access controls in accordance with this policy and any updated guidance from Federal authoritative sources;
Monitor the effectiveness of access controls, take corrective action when appropriate, and submit monitoring reports as required;
Review system audit records for indications of inappropriate usage and report findings to designated organizational officials, as specified in internal procedures; and
Generate and archive documentation upon request or as established in procedures to provide evidence of compliance with this policy.
Users will:
Have and maintain a current, favorably adjudicated background investigation in accordance with Federal requirements prior to gaining access to an information system;
conditions: prior to gaining access to an information system

policy_statements.source_text: Complete annual training for information security awareness and protecting personally identifiable information, per DR 3545-001, and sign the rules of behavior and an acceptable use agreement;
policy_statements.target: rules of behavior and an acceptable use agreement

policy_statements.source_text: Complete annual specialized role-based information security training specific to their roles or duties, if designated as having significant security responsibilities;
conditions: if designated as having significant security responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: Review DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, annually;
conditions: annually

policy_statements.source_text: Notify their supervisor if an access control vulnerability or policy violation is discovered or suspected;
conditions: if an access control vulnerability or policy violation is discovered or suspected

policy_statements.source_text: Report any suspicious or unusual activity to their supervisor as soon as possible; and
Conduct remote network access activities securely and in compliance with applicable Departmental and agency policies and procedures.

policy_statements.source_text: Disciplinary or adverse action will be affected in accordance with applicable law and regulations.

policy_statements.section_title: Penalties and Disciplinary Actions for Non-Compliance
policy_statements.source_text: Such disciplinary or adverse action will be in accordance with applicable law and regulations such as OPM and OMB regulations, and the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Federal Employees of the Executive Branch, 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2635.

policy_statements.source_text: Note that an approved waiver does not bring the system into compliance with policy.
Requests for waivers:
Are an acknowledgement of a system’s non-compliance with policy and that an acceptable plan to remediate the weakness has been provided and will be implemented; and
Must be documented as indicated in CAPE-SOP-003, Plan of Action and Milestones Management Standard Operating Procedure, Revision 1.1.

Unless otherwise specified, approved policy waivers must be reviewed and renewed every fiscal year.

every fiscal year
